title: From 'Vingean Reflection Is Tractable' to Measuring Whether LLMs Trust-Calibrate Toward Stronger Successors

original_idea.body:
# From 'Vingean Reflection Is Tractable' to Measuring Whether LLMs Trust-Calibrate Toward Stronger Successors

**Problem:** Success state: an agent can safely delegate to a successor it cannot fully verify, trusting it exactly as much as warranted. The Vingean reflection problem is abstract, but a concrete sub-question is testable now: do current LLMs, when asked to delegate a task to a 'smarter' model whose reasoning they cannot fully check, calibrate their trust to actual successor reliability?

**Direction:** Set up a delegation game: a weaker open model must decide whether to accept/override answers from a stronger model on problems where ground truth is known. Measure trust calibration (does acceptance rate track the stronger model's actual accuracy across domains?) and whether the weaker model over-trusts opaque reasoning. Pure inference, two open models.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from solved Vingean reflection, a measurable precursor is calibrated trust in less-verifiable successors. Quantifying current models' miscalibration gives the formal agenda an empirical anchor and a long-horizon threat model (recursive delegation) that labs underweight.

**Relevant context:** Vingean Reflection: Open Problems (Alignment Forum); MIRI agent-foundations agenda. Connects to scalable oversight where overseers are weaker than the overseen.
